claimed_mechanism: DFDM introduces two algebraic (kinetic: none) auxiliary scalars: chi for the MOND force law (via auxiliary-Legendre potential) and s for the preferred-frame lensing slip. Both are non-propagating, so they cannot introduce ghost/strong-coupling via kinetic normalization. The frame-breaking coupling of s to acceleration is screened by e^-y, satisfying P2. Because neither field has a kinetic term, P7 (screening kills kinetic normalization) is structurally evaded: there is no propagating mode whose normalization vanishes with screening. The lensing slip is supplied by the algebraic frame-screw s, which decouples the PPN-visible alpha (proportional to e^-y) from any kinetic sector.
inequivalence_argument: DFDM is inequivalent to all dead classes because: (1) It is NOT DC-001 (local no-preferred-frame) because it has a preferred-frame coupling (s to a_mu). (2) It is NOT DC-010 (khronometric) because it has no khronon field (no timelike_background field). (3) It is NOT DC-014 (stiff vector) because s is a scalar, not a vector, and has no kinetic term (not stiff, not propagating). (4) It is NOT DC-002 (AeST) because there is no 6-DOF aether; s is a single algebraic scalar. (5) It evades P7 because there is no propagating mode whose kinetic normalization is controlled by e^-y; both fields are auxiliary (kinetic: none). (6) It evades the DC-013 slip-lock because the frame-breaking is explicit (s couples to a_mu), not locked by diffeomorphism invariance. The key novelty is the use of TWO algebraic scalars with decoupled roles: one for MOND dynamics, one for frame-breaking lensing, both non-propagating to avoid P7.
name: Dual-Frame Decoupled MOND (DFDM)
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the chi sector reproduces the MOND force law (G1) and Newtonian recovery (G2) via the auxiliary-Legendre mechanism. The s sector, being algebraic, is determined by the e^-y screened acceleration source. Because s is non-propagating, it does not contribute to the tensor sector (G3 c_T=1 is trivially satisfied by the metric). The PPN parameters alpha_1, alpha_2 are proportional to e^-y, vanishing in the Solar System (y >> 1). Lensing is provided by the frame-slip term, which is off-ray (evading DC-013) because it explicitly breaks diffeomorphism invariance via the preferred frame. The metric slip eta is determined by the s-sector contribution, which is independent of the MOND strength (chi sector), satisfying the core cooking rule.
